column2: Themes: recurring patterns, not a status list [SO5]
column6: Two or three patterns, each seen in more than one event during the term and each with a cause in how the team works (communication, decision-making, workload, review habits), written as themes rather than the session's raw notes.
column9: Patterns are named, but there is only one or there are more than three, at least one is a single event rather than a pattern, or a cause names nothing about how the team works.
column12: A list of what happened during the term, with no synthesis into patterns.

column6: Every theme carries at least one artifact (a pull request, a board snapshot, a legible decision thread) with a caption saying what it shows. Private links include a snippet graders can read.
column9: Most themes carry an artifact, or a caption states what the artifact is rather than what it shows.
column12: Themes are asserted with no artifacts, or the artifacts cannot be opened by a grader.

column3: three, each owned, time-bound, with a recognition cue, and traceable to a theme
column6: Three actions, each with a single named owner, a timeframe, a plain-language recognition cue for how the team will know it is working, and a visible trace back to one of the themes.
column9: Three actions, but an owner is "the team", a timeframe is missing, or a recognition cue is not something anyone could observe.
column12: Fewer than three actions, or actions with no owner, no timing, and no connection to a theme.

column2: Individual pages: wins, gaps, one checkable commitment [SO3]
column3: wins and gaps tied to concrete examples, plus one checkable commitment, per student
column6: Every student has a labeled page with one or two wins and one or two gaps, each tied to a concrete example (a pull request, a review, a decision they drove or dodged), plus one winter commitment that says what the student will do differently, how progress will be visible, and by when.
column9: Pages are present for every student, but a win or gap names no example, or the commitment leaves out what the student will do differently, how progress will be visible, or by when.
column12: A student's page is missing, or the page is general reflection with no examples and no commitment. Scored per student, so this costs that student rather than the team.

column2: Writing: length, sections, claims tied to examples [SO3]
column6: Within 2 pages of team content, sectioned by heading, and every claim names the example it rests on.
column12: Two or more of the three missing.
